title: Customizing Your Site
excerpt: Discover how to customize Birkly to match your needs. From templates to styling, make Birkly work exactly the way you want.
content:
One of Birkly's greatest strengths is its flexibility. Whether you want to customize the appearance, extend functionality, or create a completely unique content management experience, Birkly provides the tools you need.

The Template System

Birkly uses a simple, natural templating language that's easy to learn yet powerful enough for complex layouts. The template syntax supports:

  • Loops: Iterate over collections and arrays
  • Conditionals: Show or hide content based on data
  • Filters: Format dates, escape HTML, and more
  • Variables: Access any data from your entries

For example, to loop through blog posts, you simply write:

{for each entry in 'blog'}
  <h2>{{ entry.title }}</h2>
  <p>{{ entry.excerpt }}</p>
{endfor}

This natural syntax makes templates readable and maintainable, even for non-developers.

Styling Your Frontend

Since Birkly is file-based, you have complete control over your frontend styling. You can use any CSS framework, preprocessor, or custom styling approach you prefer. The demo blog uses a simple, clean CSS file that you can modify or replace entirely.

For the admin panel, Birkly uses CSS variables that make theming straightforward. You can customize colors, fonts, spacing, and more by simply overriding CSS variables in a custom stylesheet.

Extending Functionality

Custom Fieldtypes

If the built-in fieldtypes don't meet your needs, you can create custom ones. Custom fieldtypes are PHP classes that define how a field is rendered in the editor and how its data is stored. This allows you to add specialized inputs for your specific use case.

Plugins

The plugin system allows you to extend Birkly with additional functionality. Plugins can add new API endpoints, modify the admin interface, add custom workflows, or integrate with external services.

Configuration Options

Birkly offers various configuration options through settings files. You can customize:

  • Site name and metadata
  • API endpoints and permissions
  • File upload limits and allowed types
  • Default content structures
  • And much more

Best Practices for Customization

  • Start simple: Use built-in features before creating custom solutions
  • Document changes: Keep notes on customizations for future reference
  • Version control: Track all customizations in your version control system
  • Test thoroughly: Always test customizations in a development environment first

With these customization options, Birkly can adapt to nearly any content management need. Start with the basics, and gradually add customizations as your requirements evolve.
